subject: Chemistry
central_question: How are spontaneous redox reactions converted into electrical energy, and how can electrical measurements predict and drive chemical change?
in_scope_units: Electrochemical cells and conversion between galvanic and electrolytic operation.
Galvanic cells, half-cells, salt bridge, cell notation, electrode potential and cell emf.
Standard hydrogen electrode and standard electrode potentials.
Nernst equation for electrode and cell potentials under non-standard conditions.
Relations among cell potential, Gibbs energy and equilibrium constant.
Conductance of electrolytic solutions: resistance, resistivity, conductivity and molar conductivity.
Measurement of conductivity, concentration dependence and Kohlrausch’s law.
Electrolytic cells, Faraday’s laws and products of electrolysis.
Primary and secondary batteries, fuel cells and corrosion.
banned_topics: Detailed redox balancing methods outside the cell reactions used here.
Chemical kinetics of electrode reactions and overpotential, which are beyond the chapter.
Semiconductor conductivity, which belongs to solid-state electronics rather than ionic solutions.

known_pitfalls.claim: Oxidation always occurs at the positive electrode.
known_pitfalls.correction: Oxidation occurs at the anode; the anode is negative in a galvanic cell but positive in an electrolytic cell.

known_pitfalls.claim: The potential of a single isolated half-cell can be measured absolutely.
known_pitfalls.correction: Only a potential difference can be measured; electrode potentials are assigned relative to the standard hydrogen electrode.

known_pitfalls.claim: Conductivity and molar conductivity both decrease on dilution.
known_pitfalls.correction: Conductivity decreases on dilution, but molar conductivity increases because ions move more freely and weak electrolytes ionise more.

known_pitfalls.claim: Multiplying a half-reaction multiplies its electrode potential.
known_pitfalls.correction: Electrode potential is an intensive quantity and is not multiplied when the equation is multiplied.

known_pitfalls.claim: A positive standard cell potential means the reverse reaction is spontaneous.
known_pitfalls.correction: A positive E°cell corresponds to negative ΔG° and spontaneity of the cell reaction as written.

recommended_example_progression: Begin with the Daniell-cell calculation in the text: E°cell = 0.34 − (−0.76) = 1.10 V.
Use NCERT Example 2.2 to apply the Nernst equation to a complete cell.
Use NCERT Example 2.3 to connect E°cell with ΔG° and K.
Apply NCERT Examples 2.4–2.6 to conductivity, molar conductivity and Kohlrausch’s law.
Use NCERT Examples 2.7–2.10 for Faraday-law and electrolysis calculations.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The end-of-chapter Exercises are numbered 2.1 to 2.18 and cover electrode potentials, Nernst equation, equilibrium, conductivity, Kohlrausch’s law, electrolysis, batteries and corrosion.
